findings.observation: value.js maintains a LOCAL FORK of glass-ui's `useLayerTransition` for its dock, and the fork implements the exact FLIP-width + CSS-transition algorithm AX.W01 names as the root cause of the dock desync. The fork's own header docstring spells out steps 1-6 (capture width → pin → swap classes → nextTick measure → animate via CSS transition → clear on transitionend) — the box-leads-content mechanism. It exists because glass-ui's `/dock` subpath barrel does NOT re-export `useLayerTransition` (only the components + `useDockState`/`dockContext`), so the consumer literally cannot import the upstream primitive and forked it. When AX.W01/W02 re-derive the morph to one-scalar one-clock, this fork stays a divergent legacy island and never inherits the fix.

findings.observation: value.js's gh-pages PRODUCTION build dist-resolves glass-ui (the `production` export condition), where the published `dist/styles/index.css` carries `@source "../components"` — which resolves to `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components`, a directory that DOES NOT EXIST (the dist is a flat `dist/*.js` chunk set, no `components/` subtree). So glass-ui's component-template content-scan scans nothing in the consumer's production build, and value.js has NO compensating `@source "...glass-ui/dist"` directive of its own. The result is the exact CLAUDE.md-documented silent-failure class: glass-ui's layout/CVA utility classes that value.js's own templates don't also emit are dropped from the production CSS — across 181 glass-ui component mount sites. This is jointly a glass-ui dist-packaging defect (the `@source ../components` is dead in dist) and a value.js consumer gap (missing the binding `@source` directive CLAUDE.md mandates).

result.slice: constellation-warp-design (AX dimension D3) — §15 click-to-warp generalized as a reusable /constellation interaction (folds into AX.W17)

findings.observation: PREMISE CORRECTION (load-bearing for the whole spec): §15 / REQUIREMENTS:183-188 assert click-to-warp 'First shipped in the slides constellation' and frame W17 as GENERALIZING an existing slides feature. It does not exist. A grep across both repos for warpTo|nearest|closest.*lattice|snapToNode returns ZERO implementation hits in any src file; the only matches are the AX REQUIREMENTS prose itself. The slides constellation.ts has NO click-to-warp — its only position-mutation is the auto-retargeting drift() (slides constellation.ts:174-195) that re-anchors the pinned anomaly node[0] on a 6-14s jittered cadence via easeInOutQuad, NOT on click. So W17's warp is NET-NEW DESIGN, not a port. The spec must say so explicitly or the implementer will hunt for a non-existent slides source.
findings.evidence: grep proof: warpTo|nearest|snapToNode|closest.*lattice across /Users/mkbabb/Programming/slides/src + /Users/mkbabb/Programming/glass-ui/src = 0 hits; slides constellation.ts:174-195 (drift, the only mutator); REQUIREMENTS.md:183-188
findings.action: In AX.W17 scope, restate §15 as 'AUTHOR (net-new) the click-to-warp interaction' and DELETE the 'generalize the slides hack' framing. Cite slides drift() as the architectural ANALOG (same node-position-mutation class) the warp shares an escape with, not as a source to port. This removes a wild-goose-chase from next session.

findings.observation: The neutral engine (constellationField.ts) has NO focal/anomaly concept whatsoever — the focal node is 100% consumer skin painted in drawOverlay. seedField() pins nothing (constellationField.ts:113-133, comment 'No node is pinned'), and ConstellationField exposes nodes as read-only-by-convention. drawOverlay is a pure PAINT pass: (ctx, field, now) => void run AFTER the four neutral passes (Constellation.vue:134-135). It CANNOT mutate node position — and warp IS node-position mutation. The W17 spec already names this exact gap: 'The one mechanic drawOverlay cannot express (anomaly DRIFT — it mutates node position) gets a documented escape' (AX.md:626-627). Warp is the SAME class as drift; it must be resolved by the SAME escape, not a second parallel one. The spec currently treats warp (§15→W17) and the drift-escape (W17 §3) as separate sentences without connecting them.
findings.evidence: constellationField.ts:113-133 (seedField pins nothing), Constellation.vue:134-135 (drawOverlay runs last, void return), AX.md:626-627 (the drift escape sentence)
findings.action: W17 must UNIFY warp + drift under ONE first-class focal-node seam, since both mutate node position and drawOverlay structurally cannot. Decide the seam shape (a focal-node descriptor with a position spring the engine steps) BEFORE the spec, not after. Without this, warp gets bolted on as a slides hack again — the exact anti-pattern §15 forbids.

findings.observation: CRITICAL spring-integration constraint missed by the spec: the constellation does NOT use Vue's useSpring composable and CANNOT. The field steps inside useCanvas2D's single shared rAF via a manual per-frame call (Constellation.vue:124 stepField(field, k, speed, livePointer)); the substrate owns the loop and steps nothing reactive. Vue's useSpring (src/composables/motion/useSpring.ts) wraps keyframes.js SpringProgress.play() which spawns ITS OWN rAF bound to a reactive Ref — using it for warp would mean a SECOND rAF outside the parked-substrate contract (defeating the offscreen/tab-hidden/PRM freeze the whole substrate exists to provide) plus a reactive ref the field-step has to read every frame. The correct primitive is a dt-stepped analytic critically-damped integrator advanced INSIDE the field step (a warpStep(field, dt) co-located with stepField), seeded with (response, dampingFraction) — the SpringProgress MATH without its rAF ownership. The spec must specify this or the implementer reaches for useSpring and breaks the park contract.
findings.evidence: Constellation.vue:118-139 (manual stepField inside the substrate render hook, no useSpring), useCanvas2D.ts:135-146 (substrate owns the single rAF + reduced-motion gate), useSpring.ts:79-96 (SpringProgress.play owns its own rAF + reactive ref)
findings.action: Specify the warp spring as a dt-stepped 2nd-order critically-damped integrator (x += v*dt; v += (-2*zeta*omega*v - omega^2*(x-target))*dt with omega=2*PI/response) advanced inside stepField/a new warpStep, reusing the keyframes.js (response, dampingFraction) param model but NOT useSpring's rAF. Per-axis (x,y) springs on the focal node. now-delta gives dt (clamp to ~50ms for tab-throttle resilience). Explicitly forbid useSpring here in the spec.

findings.observation: Nearest-lattice-point search is under-specified and has a naming ambiguity §15 itself conflates. §15 says warp goes 'to the CLOSEST lattice point to the cursor.' But 'lattice point' in a proximity-graph constellation is ambiguous: (a) the nearest existing drifting NODE to the cursor, or (b) a synthetic grid point. The constellation has NO fixed lattice — every node drifts (seedField gives all nodes random velocity). So 'lattice point' must mean (a) the nearest NODE. The search is a trivial O(count) min-distance scan over field.nodes (count default 64, ~64 hypot calls — negligible; no spatial index needed, matching the existing O(count²) edge pass at README:186). Edge case: the focal node should be EXCLUDED from its own candidate set, and a degenerate (cursor exactly on focal) should no-op. The spec names neither.
findings.evidence: REQUIREMENTS.md:184 ('CLOSEST lattice point'), seedField constellationField.ts:121-131 (all nodes drift, no fixed lattice), README.md:186 (O(count²) already accepted at count<=96)
findings.action: Specify nearestNode(field, px, py, excludeIdx): linear min-d² scan over field.nodes excluding the current focal index, returning the target node index (or its live x/y snapshot at click-time). Define behavior when the nearest node is the focal node itself (no-op) and when count is degenerate. State explicitly 'lattice point = nearest drifting node' to kill the §15 wording ambiguity.

findings.observation: TARGET-IS-MOVING problem unaddressed: the warp destination (nearest node) is itself a drifting node that keeps moving during the ~0.4-0.6s spring settle. If the spring targets a frozen click-time snapshot, the focal mark lands NEXT TO the now-moved target node (visually wrong — the whole point is it warps TO a lattice node). If it targets the live node position every frame, the spring chases a moving target (correct, and springs handle this natively — it is exactly useSpring's 'track a live target' design). This is the single most important behavioral decision in the warp and the spec is silent on it.
findings.evidence: stepField constellationField.ts:147-165 (every non-focal node drifts every frame), useSpring.ts:79-83 ('Track a LIVE numeric target with iOS-style spring physics' — the intended pattern)
findings.action: Specify LIVE-TARGET tracking: store the target node INDEX (not a position snapshot); each frame the warp spring re-reads field.nodes[targetIdx].{x,y} as its live target so it chases the drifting node and arrives ON it. On settle (|x-target| & |v| below threshold), optionally PIN the focal node onto the target (merge) or keep it as an independent settled mark — decide and state which.

findings.observation: API SEAM is genuinely undecided and the spec must pick one of three shapes — drawOverlay (paint-only) cannot carry it. The three candidates: (1) defineExpose a warpTo(clientX, clientY) | warpTo(point) imperative method on Constellation.vue (consumer calls it from its own @click handler — matches the existing defineExpose({field}) at Constellation.vue:179); (2) a built-in pointer seam: a new prop warpOnClick?: boolean that, when set, wires the host pointerdown (the same listener already added at Constellation.vue:175 for ripples) to warp the focal node automatically; (3) a focal-node DESCRIPTOR prop (focal?: { index, warp: 'click' }) the engine owns. The README's whole architecture is 'library owns field math, consumer owns chrome via drawOverlay' (README:170-181) — warp mutates field math, so it belongs library-side, which favors (2) or (3). But the FOCAL NODE itself is consumer chrome (drawOverlay), creating a split-brain: the consumer owns WHICH node is focal (it paints it) but the library must own its POSITION (to warp it). This tension is the core design problem and is unspecified.
findings.evidence: Constellation.vue:179 (defineExpose({field}) — the existing imperative seam), Constellation.vue:168-176 (the existing host pointerdown ripple listener — the seam warp would join), README.md:170-181 (the math/chrome split invariant)
findings.action: RESOLVE the split-brain in W17 by promoting the FOCAL NODE to a first-class library concept: add an optional focal node to ConstellationField (a focalIndex + a per-axis warp spring the engine steps), expose warpTo(point) via defineExpose AND/OR a warpOnClick prop, and let drawOverlay PAINT the focal node at its engine-owned position (field.nodes[field.focalIndex]). The consumer keeps the SKIN (red ring, callout); the library owns the POSITION + spring. Pick warpTo(point) imperative as the canonical low-level seam and warpOnClick as the sugar; document both.

findings.observation: REDUCED-MOTION + PARK contract interaction unspecified. The substrate freezes under prefers-reduced-motion (paints one static frame then parks; useCanvas2D.ts:284-287) and the field only steps when !handle.reducedMotion (Constellation.vue:122). Pointer reactivity (and thus the click seam) is wholly disabled under reduced-motion (Constellation.vue:144). So warp must either (a) be disabled under reduced-motion like ripples/steer (consistent, simplest), or (b) snap-to-target instantly under reduced-motion (useSpring's own PRM fast-path, useSpring.ts respectReducedMotion default true — snaps rather than springs). A click that does nothing under PRM is acceptable per the existing pattern but should be a STATED decision, not an accident. Also: a warp in progress when the surface scrolls offscreen → the substrate parks the rAF (off-screen reason), freezing the warp mid-flight; on resume the dt-delta will be huge (clamp needed, reinforcing finding on dt clamp).
findings.evidence: useCanvas2D.ts:284-287 (PRM static-frame park), Constellation.vue:122,144 (step + pointer both gated on !reducedMotion), useSpring.ts respectReducedMotion (snap fast-path)
findings.action: State the PRM policy: warp follows the ripple/steer precedent (disabled under reduced-motion — the click does not warp; the focal node stays put). Add a dt clamp (~50ms max) in warpStep so a park/resume or tab-throttle gap does not teleport the spring. Note the offscreen-park-mid-warp case resolves for free once dt is clamped + live-target tracked.

findings.observation: Coordinate-mapping + deck-scale correctness is a real hazard the spec must inherit, not re-derive. The slides constellation maps viewport pointer → canvas-local px via getBoundingClientRect (slides constellation.ts:153-161, 164-171) so the mapping stays correct under a deck CSS-scale transform; the glass-ui component does the same (Constellation.vue:145-152 toLocal). warpTo MUST go through this same getBoundingClientRect mapping for a click point — a naive clientX/Y offset would be wrong under any CSS scale/zoom (the exact slides use case). The nearestNode search then runs in canvas-local px space (field.nodes are canvas-local). The spec should reuse the existing toLocal helper, not author a parallel mapper.
findings.evidence: Constellation.vue:145-152 (toLocal: getBoundingClientRect → canvas-local px), slides constellation.ts:153-171 (the same mapping for pointer + ripple), README.md:163-165 (the deck-scale correctness rationale)
findings.action: Specify warpTo(clientX, clientY) reuses the existing toLocal mapping (getBoundingClientRect) so the click point lands in canvas-local px before the nearestNode scan; warpTo(point) accepting already-local px is the lower primitive. Cite the deck-scale invariant (README:163-165) so the implementer does not regress it.

findings.observation: Slides adoption coupling: W17 wants slides to adopt the warp and delete its local constellation.ts. But the slides anomaly is currently node[0] PINNED at a data-anomaly anchor with auto-drift (slides constellation.ts:143-150, 174-195). To adopt the generalized warp, slides must: (1) move its anomaly skin to drawOverlay reading field.focalIndex (already the W17 plan for the ring/callout), AND (2) replace its bespoke drift() with the engine's focal-node spring (so drift becomes 'warp to a periodically-chosen random node' — drift and warp UNIFY as 'spring the focal node to a target node', differing only in what picks the target: a timer vs a click). This is the cleanest possible convergence and should be stated as the W17 design thesis: drift = auto-target warp; click-warp = pointer-target warp; ONE spring, two target sources.
findings.evidence: slides constellation.ts:143-150 (anomaly node[0] pinned), 174-195 (drift = easeInOutQuad auto-retarget to a random nearby anchor), AX.md:620-627 (W17 wants the drawOverlay skin + delete slides constellation.ts)
findings.action: Make the W17 design thesis explicit: 'ONE focal-node position spring; the target is set by either a click (warpTo) or a periodic auto-pick (drift). Drift and warp are the same mechanic with different target sources.' Spec the engine to own a focal spring + a pluggable target-picker; slides' drift becomes the auto-picker variant. This satisfies the 'documented escape for drift' (AX.md:626) AND warp in one seam — zero duplication, the precept-correct convergence.

findings.observation: Settle/arrival semantics + the 'snap to closest point' vs 'interpolate to cursor' tension. §15 says warp goes to the closest lattice point AND 'smoothly interpolates there (spring/eased path, not a snap)'. These are compatible (spring TO the node) but the spec must define ARRIVAL: does the focal node (a) become the target node (identity merge — the two are now one node, the focal mark rides the target's drift thereafter), or (b) settle AT the target's position but remain a distinct node that then resumes its own behavior? Option (a) is cleaner narratively (the anomaly 'jumps to' a real lattice node and lives there) and matches the slides pinned-anomaly model. The spec is silent; this determines whether the focal node count is conserved and how the next warp originates.

result.notes:
SCOPE: This is design analysis for the §15 click-to-warp slice. READ-ONLY; no edits made.

BOTTOM LINE for next session: warp folds ENTIRELY into AX.W17 (no new wave — same FileBounds as the existing W17 constellation port). But the W17 spec must resolve FIVE undecided design questions before it can be written, and three of them are blockers:

1. (blocker) drawOverlay is paint-only and CANNOT mutate node position — warp + drift must unify under ONE first-class engine-owned focal-node seam (a focalIndex + per-axis position spring the engine steps). The W17 spec already half-acknowledges this with its 'drift escape' sentence (AX.md:626) but never connects warp to it.
2. (blocker) The warp spring must be a dt-stepped analytic integrator INSIDE the field step — NOT Vue's useSpring (which owns its own rAF and would break the substrate's offscreen/PRM park contract). Reuse keyframes.js SpringProgress MATH (response, dampingFraction) without its rAF.
3. (blocker) The API seam is genuinely undecided: warpTo(point) imperative via defineExpose vs a warpOnClick prop vs a focal-descriptor prop. The math/chrome split-brain (consumer owns WHICH node is focal via drawOverlay, library must own its POSITION to warp it) is the core tension. Recommended: promote the focal node to a library concept (focalIndex + spring), expose warpTo(point) as the canonical seam + warpOnClick as sugar, let drawOverlay paint at the engine-owned position.

THE ELEGANT CONVERGENCE (the design thesis to drive the spec): drift and warp are THE SAME mechanic — 'spring the focal node toward a target node' — differing only in what picks the target (a periodic timer for drift, a click for warp). One focal spring + a pluggable target-picker resolves §15's warp AND W17's 'documented drift escape' AND the slides-deletes-constellation.ts goal in a single seam. This is the precept-correct (DRY/KISS, no slides hack) answer and should be stated as W17's headline.

PREMISE CORRECTION: §15's claim that warp 'first shipped in the slides constellation' is FALSE (grep-proven across both repos). Warp is net-new; the slides drift() is the architectural analog, not a source to port. State this in W17 so next session does not hunt for a non-existent source.

MINOR-but-must-state: nearest-NODE search (not 'lattice point' — no fixed lattice exists; all nodes drift) is a trivial O(count) scan excluding the focal node; LIVE-TARGET tracking (target the node INDEX so the spring chases the drifting node and arrives ON it, not beside it); reuse the existing getBoundingClientRect toLocal mapping for deck-scale correctness; dt-clamp ~50ms for park/throttle resilience; PRM policy = disabled-like-ripples; arrival = identity-ride (focal re-points to the chosen node and tracks its drift). Add a π-lane warp-centroid-converges-to-a-node gate (templated on AX.W15's blob pointer-centroid gate) + a live spring-glide audit.
